title: नाट्यरचना र त्यसको प्रस्तुति {Dramatic composition and its presentation}
nepali: नाटक प्रदर्शनकारी कला हो । प्रदर्शन तथा प्रस्तुतितिर उन्मूख हुनु यसको विधागत मूल विशेषता हो । यसै कारणले गर्दा यो साहित्यको अन्य विधाभन्दा फरक छ । नाटककारले त्यसको प्रस्तुति पक्षको शिल्पीय उपकरणलाई पनि ध्यान दिएर नाट्यरचना गर्नुपर्दछ । नाट्यरचना हुनुलाई त्यसको प्रस्तुति तर्फको यात्रा आरम्भ मानिन्छ । त्यस यात्रालाई तय गर्न त्यहाँ अनेक सिद्धहस्तको सिर्जनाशील कल्पनाशीलता, समन्वय, धैर्य, तपस्या, लगनशीलता, परिश्रम, सहयोग, व्यवस्थापन आदिको आवश्यकता पर्दछ । प्रस्तुतिको केन्द्रीय सूत्र मानिने निर्देशकको जिम्मेवारी व्यवस्थापन आदिले गर्दा नाट्यरचनाले नाट्य छनोटदेखि रिहर्सल हुँदै अन्तिम प्रदर्शनका लागि दर्शकमाझ मञ्चमा प्रस्तुत हुन्छ । यस लेखमा नाट्यरचना प्रस्तुतिको क्रममा के कसरी परिमार्जित र संशोधित अवस्थामा दर्शकसामु आउंछ भन्ने कुराको अध्ययन गरिएको छ । कृतिलाई परिवर्तित, संशोधित र नाटकीय रूपान्तरण गरेर आजकाल विभिन्न विधाजस्तै कविता, कथा, उपन्यास आदिलाई मञ्चन गर्ने गरिएको पाइन्छ तर यस लेखमा केवल नाट्यरचनाको प्रस्तुतीकरण र त्यसमा देखिने परिवर्तनको अवस्थालाई अध्ययनको क्षेत्र निर्धारण गरिएको छ । नाटकको रचना शब्दका माध्यमबाट साहित्यिक रूप प्रदान गर्ने अवस्था हो भने मञ्चमा प्रस्तुत गर्नु  त्यसलाई व्यावहारिक रूपमा कार्यान्वयन गर्नु  हो । यस क्रममा नाटकको गौण कथानको काँटछाँट गौण पात्रको अप्रस्तुति, रङ्गसामग्रीको प्रयोग आदिको अवस्थामा निर्देशकले आवश्यवताअनुसार मूल नाटकीय कथ्य नमर्नेगरी परिमार्जन गरेर प्रस्तुत गर्न सक्तछन् भन्ने नै यस लेखको मूल निचोड हो ।
american_english: Drama is a performing art. Being oriented toward performance and presentation is its fundamental generic characteristic. For this very reason, it is distinct from other genres of literature. A playwright must compose a dramatic work while also paying attention to the technical craft tools of its presentation aspect. The writing of a drama is regarded as the start of the journey toward its presentation. To complete that journey requires the creative imagination, coordination, patience, dedication, perseverance, hard work, cooperation, and management of numerous seasoned practitioners. Due to the managerial responsibility of the director, who is regarded as the central nexus of production, a dramatic work travels from play selection through rehearsals to being staged before an audience for final performance. In this article, a study has been made of how and in what modified and revised form a dramatic work appears before the audience during staging. Nowadays, various genres such as poetry, stories, and novels are staged by altering, revising, and dramatically adapting works, but this article delimits its scope of study solely to the presentation of dramatic works and the state of changes seen in them. While composing a drama is the state of providing literary form through words, staging it is putting it into practical implementation. The core conclusion of this article is that in this process, in situations such as pruning minor plotlines, omitting minor characters, and utilizing stage props, the director can modify and present the work as needed without extinguishing the core dramatic message.

informal_english: Drama is a performing art, pure and simple. Being geared right towards performance and putting on a show is its core hallmark. That's the very reason it stands apart from any other literary genre. A playwright has to pen the play while keeping a sharp eye on the craft tools needed for staging it too. Getting the script written down is just the start of the trek towards putting it on stage. To complete that journey, you need the creative imagination, coordination, patience, devotion, sheer hard graft, cooperation, and management of plenty of clever hands. Thanks to the management duties of the director, who acts as the central anchor of the show, a dramatic work goes from initial play selection through rehearsals right onto the stage in front of the audience for the final performance. This paper takes a look at how and in what tweaked and revised shape a dramatic piece turns up before the audience during staging. Nowadays folks adapt poetry, short stories, and novels for the stage by altering and revising texts, but this paper keeps its scope strictly on the staging of dramatic scripts and the shifts seen during production. Penning a play gives it literary form through words, but putting it on stage is putting the thing into real practical action. The main takeaway of this paper is that throughout this process, when trimming wee minor plotlines, dropping secondary characters, or sorting out stage props, the director can adjust and stage the work as needed without killing off the heart of the dramatic message.
